knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")

```{r setup, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
library(hsc19)
library(Seurat)
library(ggplot2)
set.seed(1337)
```

## Summary

This vignette decomposes bulk RNA-seq profiles from AML leukemic stem cells
(LSCs) into nineteen gene regulatory programs and compares their ability to
predict treatment response with the supplied genetic and transcriptomic scores.
Two outcomes are considered: venetoclax-based treatment (`response_vv`) and
DA treatment (`response_da`), as annotated in the study metadata.

## Data preparation

The inputs for the Renders dataset (ArrayExpress accession
[E-MTAB-14142](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/biostudies/arrayexpress/studies/E-MTAB-14142))
are included in `data_Venetoclax/`: the count matrix, the study sample annotations
(`E-MTAB-14142.sdrf.txt`), and the supplementary scores
(`Metadata_Lars_10022026.csv`). We use the original study annotations for both
response outcomes and the supplementary table for the comparison scores.
Only diagnostic LSC samples are retained. Sequencing lanes are deduplicated
using the sample-level columns of the annotation table.

```{r prepare-data, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
study_metadata <- read.delim(
  "data_Venetoclax/E-MTAB-14142.sdrf.txt", check.names = FALSE,
  na.strings = c("", "NA")
)
study_metadata <- unique(study_metadata[, seq_len(10)])
study_metadata <- subset(
  study_metadata,
  `Characteristics[cell type]` == "LSC" &
    `Characteristics[disease staging]` == "Diagnosis"
)

scores <- read.csv(
  "data_Venetoclax/Metadata_Lars_10022026.csv", check.names = FALSE,
  na.strings = c("", "NA")
)
join_columns <- c(
  "Characteristics[individual]", "Comment[ENA_SAMPLE]", "Source Name",
  "Characteristics[cell type]", "Characteristics[disease staging]"
)
score_columns <- c("3GeneScore", "New Score", "Mode-AML", "ELN-2022",
                   "PDX", "MAC-Score_LSC")
meta <- merge(study_metadata, scores[, c(join_columns, score_columns)],
              by = join_columns)
names(meta)[match(score_columns, names(meta))] <-
  c("threegene", "newscore", "modeaml", "eln2022", "PDX", "MAC")
rownames(meta) <- with(meta, paste(
  `Characteristics[individual]`, `Characteristics[cell type]`,
  `Characteristics[disease staging]`, sep = "_"
))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(rownames(meta)))

counts <- read.csv(
  "data_Venetoclax/Count_matrix_LSC_MATURE.csv.gz", row.names = 1,
  check.names = FALSE
)
stopifnot(all(rownames(meta) %in% colnames(counts)))
counts <- as.matrix(counts[, rownames(meta), drop = FALSE])

s <- CreateSeuratObject(counts, meta.data = meta)
s <- NormalizeData(s, verbose = FALSE)
s <- FindVariableFeatures(s, verbose = FALSE)
s <- ScaleData(s, verbose = FALSE)
meta <- meta[colnames(s), , drop = FALSE]

meta$response_vv <- meta$`Characteristics[response_vv]` == "responder"
meta$response_da <- meta$`Characteristics[response_da]` == "responder"
meta$threegene <- factor(meta$threegene, levels = c("Low", "Medium", "High"))
meta$newscore <- factor(meta$newscore, levels = c("Favorable", "Adverse"))
meta$threegene_num <- as.integer(meta$threegene)
meta$newscore_num <- as.integer(meta$newscore)
has.vv <- rownames(meta)[!is.na(meta$response_vv)]
has.da <- rownames(meta)[!is.na(meta$response_da)]
```

## Decompose data into GRPs

```{r decompose}
result <- decompose(s = s)
print(result)
```

## Associate GRPs with treatment response

Each analysis includes all samples with a recorded outcome. Missing comparison
scores are omitted only from the models requiring those scores, so GRP models
can still use all outcome-annotated samples. The numeric scores encode their
ordered risk categories. The custom models below treat the scores as categorical
or continuous predictors according to their original type.

The association functions report Wilcoxon tests and compare out-of-fold ROC
AUCs over ten repeated cross-validation runs. They use ten folds for more than
50 samples and leave-one-out cross-validation for smaller cohorts. The standard
deviations describe variation across repeats, rather than confidence intervals.
The calculations can take several minutes; reduce `cores` for machines with
fewer available CPUs.

```{r associate}
models <- c("threegene", "eln2022", "newscore", "MAC")
names(models) <- c("3 Gene score", "ELN22 risk", "New Score", "MAC Score")
other_predictors <- c("threegene_num", "newscore_num")

grp2output_vv <- associate_binary_outcome(
  subset(result, include = has.vv), meta[has.vv, , drop = FALSE],
  "response_vv", other.predictors = other_predictors,
  run.ML = TRUE, replicates = 10, cores = 10, arbitrary.models = models
)
saveRDS(grp2output_vv, file = "grp2output_vv.rds")
# grp2output_da <- associate_binary_outcome(
#   subset(result, include = has.da), meta[has.da, , drop = FALSE],
#   "response_da", other.predictors = other_predictors,
#   run.ML = TRUE, replicates = 10, cores = 10
# )
```

```{r sample-numbers}
data.frame(
  outcome = c("VV", "DA"),
  samples = c(length(has.vv), length(has.da)),
  responders = c(sum(meta$response_vv, na.rm = TRUE),
                 sum(meta$response_da, na.rm = TRUE))
)
grp2output_vv$p.values
# grp2output_da$p.values
```

## Response by score stratum

GRP18 is oriented using the package's program annotation and divided into
tertiles. MAC scores are likewise divided into tertiles among samples with
observed VV response and MAC score. The bars show exact 90% binomial confidence
intervals; point sizes indicate the number of samples in each stratum.

```{r response-strata, fig.width=6, fig.height=3.5}
plf <- meta[has.vv, , drop = FALSE]
grp18_sign <- factor_annotation$multiply_with[
  factor_annotation$factor_id == "Factor_18"
]
strata <- c("Low", "Medium", "High")
plf$GRP18 <- factor(
  infotheo::discretize(data.frame(score =
    result@result["Factor_18", has.vv] * grp18_sign), nbins = 3)[[1]],
  levels = 1:3, labels = strata
)
plf$MAC_tertile <- NA_integer_
with_mac <- !is.na(plf$MAC)
plf$MAC_tertile[with_mac] <- infotheo::discretize(
  data.frame(score = plf$MAC[with_mac]), nbins = 3
)[[1]]
plf$MAC_tertile <- factor(plf$MAC_tertile, levels = 1:3, labels = strata)

score_names <- c(GRP18 = "GRP18 (tertiles)", threegene = "3 Gene score",
                 MAC_tertile = "MAC Score (tertiles)")
response_summary <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(score_names), function(score) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(strata, function(stratum) {
    response <- plf$response_vv[!is.na(plf[[score]]) & plf[[score]] == stratum]
    if (!length(response)) return(NULL)
    ci <- binom.test(sum(response), length(response), conf.level = 0.9)$conf.int
    data.frame(score = score_names[[score]], stratum = stratum,
               n = length(response), response = mean(response),
               lower = ci[1], upper = ci[2])
  }))
}))
response_summary$stratum <- factor(response_summary$stratum, levels = strata)

ggplot(response_summary, aes(stratum, response, color = score)) +
  geom_linerange(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper),
                 position = position_dodge(width = 0.3)) +
  geom_point(aes(size = n), position = position_dodge(width = 0.3)) +
  scale_y_continuous("Responders (%)", breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.2),
                     labels = seq(0, 100, 20), limits = c(0, 1)) +
  scale_size_area(name = "Samples", max_size = 4) +
  scale_color_brewer(palette = "Set1", name = "Predictor") +
  xlab("Stratum") + theme_bw() + theme(panel.grid = element_blank())
```

## Compare predictive performance

The best single GRP is selected within each training fold; the LASSO GRP model
combines the decomposed programs. All displayed AUCs are based on held-out
predictions. Models with missing scores may be evaluated on fewer samples.

```{r auc-plot, fig.width=6, fig.height=3}
model_labels <- c(
  AUC.best.factor = "Best single GRP", AUC.lasso.factors = "GRPs (LASSO)",
  "3 Gene score" = "3 Gene score", "ELN22 risk" = "ELN22 risk",
  "New Score" = "New Score", "MAC Score" = "MAC Score"
)
performance <- data.frame(
  model = names(grp2output_vv$aucs), auc = grp2output_vv$aucs,
  sd = grp2output_vv$aucs.sd
)
performance <- subset(performance, model %in% names(model_labels))
performance$model <- factor(performance$model, levels = rev(names(model_labels)))
ggplot(performance, aes(auc, model)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = auc - sd, xmax = auc + sd),
                orientation = "y", width = 0.1) +
  scale_y_discrete(labels = model_labels) +
  xlab("Cross-validated ROC AUC (mean ± SD)") + ylab(NULL) +
  theme_bw() + theme(panel.grid = element_blank())
```

The corresponding auPRCs use average precision, with responders as the positive
class, and summarize the same held-out predictions across CV replicates.

```{r auprc-plot, fig.width=6, fig.height=3}
pr_performance <- data.frame(
  model = names(grp2output_vv$auprcs), auprc = grp2output_vv$auprcs,
  sd = grp2output_vv$auprcs.sd
)
pr_performance <- subset(pr_performance, model %in% names(model_labels))
pr_performance$model <- factor(pr_performance$model, levels = rev(names(model_labels)))
ggplot(pr_performance, aes(auprc, model)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = auprc - sd, xmax = auprc + sd),
                orientation = "y", width = 0.1) +
  scale_y_discrete(labels = model_labels) +
  xlab("Cross-validated auPRC (mean ± SD)") + ylab(NULL) +
  theme_bw() + theme(panel.grid = element_blank())
```
